messages.content:
Build an in-browser orbital mechanics simulator

Deliver a finished, usable product, not a demo page or marketing landing page. Choose the product concept, architecture, interactions, and visual direction yourself. Use actual orbital mechanics and state the model’s assumptions and limitations.

Think through a real user's purpose, a complete workflow, and the states needed to finish it. Make consequential choices understandable and recoverable. Include useful starting conditions, explain the physics honestly, and test the numerical behavior independently of the interface. Finish the small product well rather than leaving placeholders.

Runtime packaging and verification scaffold (separate from creative direction):
- Implement from scratch. Do not inspect the prior experiment, other runs, or any pre-existing simulator implementation. Do not delegate generation to another model.
- Work only in the supplied run directory. Create index.html with optional main.js and local CSS/JavaScript modules. If using main.js, HTML must contain exactly <script type="module" src="./main.js"></script>. CSS can be imported from main.js. A single fully inline HTML file is also allowed.
- Available environment: vanilla JavaScript, optional installed Three.js 0.186.1, Vite 7.3.6, Node 24. No additional dependencies, runtime network calls, remote assets/fonts, backend, accounts, analytics, or live orbital/celestial data. Do not modify package files or shared app files. Canvas, SVG, DOM, and 3D are all allowed; Three.js is not mandatory. If using WebGL, handle unsupported graphics gracefully.
- The common harness bundles JavaScript and CSS into one inline HTML document. Its viewer is an iframe sandbox with allow-scripts and an opaque origin. Do not access parent/top, communicate across frames, or rely on persistent storage, cookies, or origin-specific APIs.
- Make one bounded implementation and its self-test/repair phase. Validate JavaScript syntax and perform an isolated Vite build with write:false. Run quantitative numerical tests applicable to your chosen mechanics, independently of the interface, and preserve a directly rerunnable test script in the run directory. Test the actual implementation's physics functions, not a separately copied formula. Record exact commands, results, tolerances, and repairs. Repair your own implementation as needed for these checks. Do not impose a tiny arbitrary token cutoff or clone existing code.
- Browser localhost access is unavailable; do not claim browser checks or bypass that restriction. Actual browser appearance, interactions, and performance remain unverified until separately reviewed.
- Include worker-report.json with product title, description, implementation start/end UTC timestamps, exact tests and outcomes, numerical assumptions and limitations, repairs, and unknowns. Set tokenUsage and cost to null unless the runtime supplies measured values. Do not invent token counts, costs, or quality scores.

Reporting-only amendment (added after the first three launches; creative prompts and runtime constraints are unchanged):
At the end of your run, include actual runtime-provided token counters if accessible: input, cached input, output, reasoning, and total. Preserve the provider's field semantics and avoid double counting. Identify the counter source and whether counts include tools or agent overhead. Do not estimate from source length or the context budget, inspect restricted session-history paths, or inspect credentials. If actual counters are inaccessible, set tokenUsage to null and give the reason. Set cost to null unless measured cost is supplied by the runtime. Do not create another inference run solely to obtain counters.

generationReport.description: A finished planar orbital workbench for learning and flying two-burn Earth-orbit transfers. Guided Hohmann planning is paired with free radial/transverse impulse previews, time controls, live telemetry, alternate starting orbits, and recoverable flight history.
generationReport.timestampSource: UTC clock obtained from the execution environment at the start of design/implementation and Date.toISOString at final report creation.
completeWorkflow: Load a circular starting orbit or use the prepared 400 km flight.
Enter a target altitude and review the predicted path, two burns, coast duration, and total delta-v.
Execute departure. Play at 1×–1,000× or jump to the exact arrival event.
Arrival automatically pauses and locks time; execute circularization or explicitly cancel the remaining plan.
Inspect final orbital elements, target-radius error, and flight log. Plan another transfer, try free maneuvers, undo, or reset.
features: Geotransfer, high-ellipse, escape, and custom starts
Transverse/radial burn components with actual post-burn conic preview
Spherical surface collision detection independent of time warp
Target editing locks, stale-plan prevention, and confirmation before discarding active flight state
20-burn undo that restores state, time, plan, and burn inputs
Flight log, period, eccentricity, speed, perigee and apogee telemetry
Canvas pan, zoom, fit, labels and vector toggles
Responsive CSS, keyboard shortcuts, dialog controls and graphic-unavailable fallback

numericalModel.propagator: Universal-variable Kepler f/g propagation. Stumpff functions use a near-zero series. Universal anomaly uses bracketed Newton iteration with relative equation tolerance 2e-11 and a 100-iteration safeguard. Bound propagation reduces elapsed time modulo the period.
numericalModel.impacts: Conic timing predicts the next inbound spherical surface encounter before an advance. The prediction is refined against the actual Kepler propagator to a 1e-6 km radius residual; surface events cannot be skipped by a large time jump.
numericalModel.maneuvers: Instantaneous impulses in a local radial/transverse frame. Positive transverse is perpendicular to radius in the current angular-momentum direction. Hohmann plans require a bound orbit with eccentricity ≤1e-4.
assumptions: Earth fixed at the origin; spacecraft mass does not affect Earth.
Planar, Newtonian two-body motion with a spherical Earth.
No drag, atmosphere, Earth oblateness/rotation, inclination, third bodies, or finite-duration thrust.
Delta-v is a velocity-change budget, not propellant mass.
Hohmann transfers are not universally globally minimum-delta-v for all radius ratios.
Earth illustration and spacecraft glyphs are decorative; Cartesian geometry and the km scale bar use physical scale.
productLimits: Custom initial and target altitudes: 120–100,000 km.
Nearly radial states with under 0.1% of local circular transverse speed are rejected.
A maximum of 20 burns can be undone; 80 latest log entries are retained.
No persistence; refreshing the tab starts over.
Rendering clips conic samples to a finite view extent; open paths have no apoapsis or period.

repairs.finding: An initially labeled outbound hyperbola used velocity [8,5] km/s at 400 km altitude, which is actually a bound state.
repairs.repair: Corrected the independent test fixture to [12,5] km/s. The model correctly predicted the original state would eventually return.
repairs.verifiedBy: Full numerical suite passed after correction.

repairs.finding: A near-parabolic bound impact case with e=0.999999999 initially stopped about 0.185 km below the spherical surface due to cancellation in mean-anomaly timing.
repairs.repair: Preserved small positive wrapped anomalies, used negative inbound eccentric anomaly, and refined predicted impacts against the production propagator.
repairs.verifiedBy: Six near-parabolic cases pass a 1e-5 km radius tolerance; 200 deterministic arbitrary-burn cases also pass. Actual maximum random impact residual was 3.697141437442042e-7 km.

repairs.finding: Code review identified that resuming time at a planned arrival could move away from the burn point while keeping the arrival maneuver active.
repairs.repair: Locked Play and +60s at arrival until the user executes or explicitly cancels the remaining plan.
repairs.verifiedBy: Node controller workflow checks for automatic pause, transport lock, completion release, and undo restoration all pass.

repairs.finding: Undo originally restored the Cartesian state and plan but did not restore manual burn input values.
repairs.repair: Burn snapshots now retain and restore both manual burn components.
repairs.verifiedBy: Node controller test verifies deliberate retry after undo.

repairs.finding: Focus-centered radius fitting wastes view space for eccentric orbits.
repairs.repair: Fit uses physical conic-sample bounds and recenters the camera around all relevant paths.
repairs.verifiedBy: JavaScript syntax and isolated build pass. Actual browser layout remains unverified.
